# Large-model joining Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Produce safe, printable, persistent joints for STL sections generated by Large Model mode.

**Architecture:** A pure joining planner describes complementary connector geometry for adjacent printable parts in millimetres. The STL splitter applies those descriptors symmetrically and validates each output mesh. `StlStudio` owns interaction state, persists durable plans against the STL asset, and reuses the existing STL/ZIP export path.

**Tech Stack:** React 18, TypeScript, Dexie, browser Blob exports, existing custom STL mesh utilities, Node assertion scripts.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-large-model-joining-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- Work only on `plans-to-print-rebuild`; do not merge or deploy production.
- Use model-space millimetres and printer-profile default clearance.
- Default join is keyed dovetail tabs plus round alignment pins; pins-only and removable clip-fit are alternatives.
- Invalid, thin-wall, out-of-bounds or stale joins must block export without altering the valid split.
- Persist only durable joining-plan data; regenerate preview meshes.
- Keep current safe mesh-cutting limits and watertight validation.

## Review Focus

- A split modified after generation must be marked stale and cannot export until regenerated.
- Exact cut boundaries or model edges must produce validation feedback, never malformed STL.
- The printer-profile clearance must survive an asset reopen and never accept non-positive or unsafe values.
- A three-or-more part split must receive complementary joins at each shared boundary, not only the first boundary.
- ZIP output must not retain the old “no connectors” warning after valid joins are generated.

---

## File structure

- Create `src/lib/printers/joinPlanner.ts`: joining modes, descriptor types, safe clearances and pure boundary planning.
- Create `src/lib/printers/joinGeometry.ts`: applies validated descriptors to split STL meshes and revalidates results.
- Modify `src/lib/printers/meshSplitter.ts`: retain split-boundary metadata and expose connector-ready parts.
- Modify `src/db/schema.ts`, `src/db/index.ts`, `src/db/repository.ts`: version and persist the durable joining plan on STL assets.
- Modify `src/components/StlStudio.tsx`: joining controls, stale state, preview labels and guarded export.
- Modify `scripts/mesh-split-tests.mjs`: geometry, safety and complementary-join tests.
- Modify `scripts/zip-export-tests.mjs`: assembly manifest/package connector-content test.

## Self-review

- Spec coverage: Tasks 1–2 implement deterministic, safe joins; Task 3 adds durable persistence/staleness; Task 4 covers UI and export; Task 5 verifies browser behaviour and all required checks.
- Type consistency: `JoiningPlan` is created by the planner, applied by geometry, persisted on `StlAsset`, and consumed by `StlStudio`.
- Review focus coverage: stale-plan check is Task 3/4; boundary safety and clearance are Task 1/2; multi-part joins are Task 1/2; ZIP copy is Task 4.
- Scope: This plan intentionally excludes arbitrary mesh repair and physical calibration.
